blocks.alt: American Voters Overwhelmingly Reject AI Data Centers

blocks.text: 在昨晚的中期选举中，全美各地民众对数据中心说了“不”。在13个州的40多场选举中，与数据中心相关的提案被明确列入选票。其中38场（且数字还在增加）的选民投票反对数据中心。六个城市投票决定彻底禁止数据中心，另有12个城市对这类建筑可使用的兆瓦数设了上限。除了具体的公投提案之外，全国范围内支持数据中心的候选人也纷纷落败。

blocks.text: 对支持数据中心政客最引人注目的否定之一发生在得克萨斯州，格雷格·阿博特（Gregg Abbott）竞选第四个州长任期失败。阿博特曾把得州打造成对数据中心友好的地方。该州有300多个正在运营的数据中心，而且计划将这个数字翻一番。“得州是AI发展的中心，”阿博特在2025年与谷歌CEO桑达尔·皮查伊（Sundar Pichai）共同出席的新闻发布会上说。“我们必须确保美国始终站在AI革命的最前沿，而得州正是实现这一目标的地方。”他随后从与数据中心相关的捐赠者那里接受了超过900万美元。

blocks.text: 反对数据中心的候选人在全国各地的州级选举中以压倒性优势获胜。在肯塔基州伯金市，市长候选人乔治·亨斯利（George Hensley）在投票批准一个超大规模项目后竞选失败——输给了一位写入式候选人。亨斯利是选票上唯一的名字，却输给了开展反数据中心写入式竞选的乔·门罗（Joe Monroe）。堪萨斯州恩波里亚市——当地警方逮捕了一名学校教师，原因是他在一场与数据中心相关的市政会议上鼓掌——通过了一项禁令，禁止高影响数据中心。在俄克拉何马州育空市，市长在支持一个超大规模数据中心项目后输掉了罢免选举。

blocks.text: “这次中期选举发出了一个明确的信号——人们不想在自己的后院看到数据中心，”Local Progress的副传播总监迈克尔·怀特塞德斯（Michael Whitesides）对404 Media说。“全国各地的人们并没有看到这些数据中心以及它们所驱动的AI在日常生活里兑现承诺的好处。他们看到的是基本商品和服务越来越贵，而这些亿万富翁支持的庞然大物占用了社区空间，污染了他们的空气，还推高了他们的水电费。”

blocks.text: 在数据中心正在建设的社区里，美国选民讨厌数据中心。它们推高电费、大量耗水，还为硅谷的 AI 机器供能。昨晚，美国否决了数据中心，既把它们视为大型科技寡头的象征，也视为其想要构建的未来的一种实体体现。这个未来，美国人似乎愿意为之抗争。

blocks.alt: American Voters Overwhelmingly Reject AI Data Centers

blocks.text: People across America rejected data centers during last night’s midterm election. Proposals related to data centers were explicitly on the ballot in more than 40 races across 13 states. People voted against data centers in 38 of them and counting. Six cities voted to ban data centers outright and 12 put limits on the amount of megawatts such buildings could draw. In addition to specific ballot measures, candidates who supported data centers lost across the country.

in 38 of them and counting. Six cities voted to ban data centers outright and 12 put limits on the amount of megawatts such buildings could draw. In addition to specific ballot measures, candidates who supported data centers lost across the country.

blocks.text: One of the most striking repudiations of pro data center politicians was in Texas, where Gregg Abbott lost a bid for a fourth term as governor. Abbott had made Texas a data center friendly place. The state has more than 300 working data centers and there are plans to double that number. “Texas is the epicenter of AI development,” Abbott said in 2025 at a press conference with Google CEO Sundar Pichai. “We must ensure that America remains at the forefront of the AI revolution, and Texas is the place where that can happen.” He went on to accept more than $9 million from data center-related donors.

blocks.text: When public sentiment turned against data centers, Abbott attempted to ride shifting political winds by issuing a “pause” on new projects. The pause wasn’t real. Texas regulators continued to approve data center projects after Abbott’s announcement and only shut down the state’s permitting web portal when 404 Media reported it.

blocks.text: Gina Hinojosa, Texas’s Democratic governor-elect, made Abbott’s stance on data centers a central part of her campaign. Abbott’s words about making Texas a data center-friendly AI state played on TVs and the internet over and over again. He lost by more than 700,000 votes.

blocks.text: Anti-data center candidates overwhelmingly won statewide races across the country. In Burgin, Kentucky, mayoral candidate George Hensley lost his bid after voting to approve a hyperscale project—to a write-in candidate. Hensley was the only name on the ballot, and he lost to Joe MonroeTK, who ran an anti-data center write-in campaign. Emporia, Kansas — where police arrested a school teacher for clapping during a data center related city meeting — passed a ban on high impact data centers. In Yukon, Oklahoma the mayor lost a recall election after he supported a hyperscale data center project.

blocks.text: "These midterms sent a clear message — people don't want to see data centers in their backyards,” Michael Whitesides, the deputy communications director for Local Progress, told 404 Media. “Across the country, people do not see the promised benefit of these data centers, and the AI they power, playing out in their daily lives. They're seeing basic goods and services get more expensive while these billionaire backed monstrosities take up space in their community, poison their air, and drive up their utility bills.”

blocks.text: Local Progress is a network of local elected officials. Over the past year, its members have become increasingly focused on data centers as a top political issue. “Last night, we saw local, state, and federal officials who backed data center deals lose their seats,” Whitesides said. He noted that Kim Rooney in Asheville, North Carolina and Amanda Rodrigues in San Marcos, Texas (both members of Local Progress) were elected mayors in their cities after running anti-data center campaigns.

blocks.text: “Big Tech will continue its typical playbook of trying to buy and bully local officials into complying with their demands for more data center development, but our hope is that last night's results are a clear signal to local leaders that they can resist and their community will back them up,” Whitesides said.

blocks.text: American voters in the communities where they’re being built hate data centers. They run up power bills, burn through water, and power Silicon Valley’s AI apparatus. America rejected data centers last night as both symbols of the big tech oligarchy and a physical manifestation of the future it wants to build. It’s a future Americans seem willing to fight.

blocks.text: Elon Musk, one of the night’s big losers, took a break from a weeks-long posting spree on X as the election results rolled in. Musk spent half a billion dollars on the midterms, $224 of it in Texas, the state where he lives and does a lot of business. The world’s richest man wanted to cover the state in data centers. Those plans aren’t looking good now that Abbott is out and Hinojoa is in.
